policy.reason: Navigation IS the egress decision: it is the moment 'fetch a page' can become 'send data somewhere', and the destination may have been chosen by text the agent read on a previous page. A human confirms it until the per-desk domain allowlist lands (phase 2), which is what turns routine browsing back into Allow while keeping the first visit to an unknown host a decision. The approval binds to the destination, not just the request: a cross-origin redirect off the approved URL is refused and named, so a server cannot pick a different address after the fact. The executor independently refuses anything that is not http/https, so javascript:, data: and file: cannot re-open the script-execution door the manifest closes.

click.displayName: Click an element on the page

policy.reason: Allowed only because the executor confines a click to the page's own origin: a link reaches any host on the internet, so allowing clicks while gating `navigate` behind approval would have made that gate decorative. EVERY cross-origin request the click causes is failed and reported — fetch, XHR, sendBeacon and image pixels as well as navigations, because a handler can send data without going anywhere — and popups cannot be created at all, so leaving the site still goes through `navigate` and a human. This bounds what the CLICK does, not what the page does once the command ends: interception lives only while a command runs, so a page can schedule a request for later, and it does not stop a click that posts to the site the agent is already on. Enforcement that outlives a command is the phase-2 egress proxy. The target is named by a reference carrying the node's identity and the role+name it had when observed, so a page that changes in between is refused rather than clicked blind; each click is audited, and the blast radius is that session's browser profile, which is deliberately not the human's.

Returning to a page already visited in this session adds no reach: it cannot reveal a host the agent has not already been to, and it is how an agent recovers from a wrong turn without a fresh navigation.
